Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/usnistgov__ssmdevices --backend fake (exit 0); gate.digest is the digest line that last run printed, and check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. The evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null, no human reviewed or tested this package, and no hardware run is claimed. Recon: the card's first entry symbol ssmdevices.instruments.attenuators:MiniCircuitsRCDAT was confirmed at src/ssmdevices/instruments/attenuators.py:13. The other card entry symbols (LocalPythonTrafficProfiler_ClosedLoopTCP and the three RohdeSchwarzFSW26 classes) are different devices and software of the same repository; this package implements only the MiniCircuitsRCDAT. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD'S HELPER: the helper hint names PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct Driver with a native.py factory, as the card's decision (direct-driver) says, because the upstream attenuation_setting is a property whose getter and setter are the device state and whose value is quantized by the device; the family grammar cannot express that property setter. The class is R1, matching the card floor: the attenuator is a passive RF component. The loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package only at R2 and R3, so that protection does not apply here and is not claimed; the hardware backend (native.py, the USB HID transport, and the upstream ssmdevices package) was never imported or run. Covered: reads of attenuation_setting, part_number and serial_number, the attenuation_setting write, and the e-stop. The write limit 0 to 115 dB is sourced from the upstream property declaration (src/ssmdevices/instruments/attenuators.py:52-54); the upstream setter keeps whole-decibel and quarter-decibel bytes (attenuators.py:78-86), so the write reports the quarter-decibel value the device stores. The e-stop drives the setting to the 115 dB maximum, the lowest RF level the attenuator can pass; the device has no separate stop command. NOT COVERED: the calibrated attenuation and calibrated output power (their values derive from the calibration table and frequency selected for the installed unit; attenuators.py:90-103), the calibration table selection (the clone ships tables under src/ssmdevices/lib/cal/), frequency, channel, output-power offset and timeout configuration, and every other device class of the clone. The card's mock_strategy is upstream-sim, but the hints point at base-station and GPS simulators that do not model this attenuator, so the fake is a package-local in-memory stand-in, not a recording, and all of its fixed values are placeholders; it models only the members the driver uses. The one Limit is sourced, so site-limits.example.json was not needed and the exemplar's copy was deleted. G4 reported no warnings. The only gate findings are four G7.MAYBE_ABSENT warnings (close, model, serial_number, open): the SDK class-surface reader does not follow the base import inside the if __name__ == '__main__' block at src/ssmdevices/instruments/attenuators.py:7-10, although SwitchAttenuatorBase is defined in src/ssmdevices/instruments/_minicircuits_usb.py:231 and the members are at _minicircuits_usb.py:35-54 and :241-249; the names therefore exist in the clone and the warning is the expected one for an unresolved base.
